3) The Complainant had filed the Criminal Application No.287 of 2021 wherein it was stated that,
Accused no.1-M/s.Bhimashankar Developers is doing the business of development of real estate,
construction and other allied activities.
Accused Nos.2 and 3 are partners of accused no.1.

In the month of August 2017, the accused persons informed the Complainant that, they have started a real estate scheme i.e., 'Investment Scheme' in respect of a land bearing Gat No.372 and 369,
Amberwadi, Khandala, Satara, wherein money invested will give lucrative returns and it will be paid at the end of two years.
In the alternative, the Complainant will have an option to retain certain plots in the said land, instead of taking back the deposited money, but upon payment of certain amount.

Relying upon the said representation and assurance, the Complainant agreed to invest Rs.15,23,000/- in the said scheme on an assurance by the accused P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL379.2023.doc.doc persons that, they would return an amount totaling Rs.1,15,92,378/- upon expiration of 24 months, in phased manner, in the form of PDCs.

In the alternative, the Complainant will have an option to retain plot Nos. 12, 14, 35, 118 and 139, offered as security/pledge, on payment of Rs.12,99,900/- at the time of handing over possession of the said plots.
Accordingly, the Complainant invested Rs.15,23,000/- in the said scheme by cheque dated 17th July, 2017.

A 'Memo of Understanding' (MoU) dated 16th August, 2017 was entered into between the parties containing the details of the invested amount, the land, the assured compensation/interest and the terms and conditions.

At the time of MoU the accused persons gave total 12 post dated cheques each of Rs.9,66,032/- for the period of 16 th August, 2019 to 17th July,
2020.
3.1) That, after expiry of the agreed two years period, the Complainant approached the accused to claim the invested amount along with the agreed returns of Rs.1,15,92,378/-.

The accused persons,
however, did not pay the said amount on the pretext of financial crisis.
Thereafter, the Complainant followed up with the accused persons to get the said amount but in vain.
At this juncture the Complainant reaslised that, the accused persons cheated her.
Therefore, she cancelled the MoU and deposited one of the said cheques for encashment, giving prior intimation to accused.
However, the said cheque dishonoured.
Thereafter, also the Complainant followed up with the accused persons to get her money along P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL379.2023.doc.doc with the benefits accrued thereon.
However, the accused persons avoided to pay the same by giving false pretext of financial crisis.
Thereafter, the Complainants learn that, the accused persons siphoned the funds of accused no.1 to other shell entities and sister companies.

Thus, the accused persons deceived the Complainant and dishonestly induced her to deposit her money by floating nonviable development scheme in respect Pushpa Zalamchand Jain vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22856810/
3 of the said land but without any intention to return the said deposited money along with the promised compensation/interest.

sentences.text:
Hence, the Complainant sent a written complaint by post to Shivaji Nagar Police Station, Pune, Commissioner of Police, Pune, Deputy Commissioner of Police,
Pune, EOW and Cyber Cell, Pune on 12 th July, 2021.
However, the police have not done any investigation in the matter.
This led to filing of Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.287 of 2021.

4) After considering the Application and the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the Complainant, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune noted that, the transaction was based on the MoU.
In the month of August 2019 itself, the Complainant knew that, the accused persons were not in a position to repay the invested amount.
One of the post dated cheques was dishonoured.
However, the Complainant persuaded with the accused for refund of her money and has not taken any steps against the accused persons for more than two year.
Lastly, she sent her complaint to Shivaji Nagar Police Station, Pune.
In this background, the P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL379.2023.doc.doc learned Judge held that, the Complainant knew that the transaction in question was of civil nature,
therefore
, till 12th July, 2021 she did not approach the police nor the Court.

Thus, the Complainant failed to make out a satisfactory ground to hold that, since beginning the accused persons had intention to cheat, therefore, it is necessary to direct the police to register the F.I.R.
Hence, the learned Judge persuaded to reject the Application.
Hence, the present Appeal.
5) Mr.Nashikkar, Advocate for the Appellant submitted that, the accused persons floated a wholly nonviable scheme of investment and returns.
This conduct manifests that, since inception there was intention on the part of accused persons to cheat the Complainant.
Therefore, the accused persons called the investment and latter on siphoned that money to shell entities/sister companies.

Thus,
this is a clear case of cheating and misappropriation.

Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, it is evident that, the amount invested in the scheme is a 'Deposit' and the accused are falling in the expression 'Financial Establishments', as defined in Section 2(c) and 2(d)
of the MPID Act, respectively.
However, the learned Judge completely ignored the above and erroneously held that, the transaction in question is of civil nature.
Therefore, the impugned Order is not sustainable in law and liable to be quashed.
To buttress his submissions, the learned Advocate placed his reliance on following decisions.
We have carefully considered the same.

P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL379.2023.doc.doc i) State of Maharashtra vs. 63 Moons Technologies  (2024) SCC OnLine SC 223,
ii) Rajiv Ramanlal Shah vs. Senior Inspector of Police Criminal Writ Petition No.1224 of 2001 dtd. 24/01/2002 iii) S. W. 4 vi) Ajay vs. State of Maharashtra Criminal Writ Petition No.108 of 2021 dated 21/10/2022 5.1)
Learned APP submitted that, considering the facts and circumstances of the case necessary Order may be passed.

sentences.text: 6) Per contra, Mr. Rajiv Chavan, learned Senior Advocate for the Respondent Nos.2 to 6 submitted that, even though, the Complainant alleged that, after expiry of the two years period she cancelled the MoU and requested for the compensation/interest amount, no notice to that effect was issued by the Complainant to the accused persons.
The Complainant did not avail the option of purchasing the proposed plots by paying the agreed balance consideration.
There is delay in filing the Application.
Therefore, the learned Additional Judge rightly held that, this is purely a civil dispute.
Hence, the rejection of the Application cannot be questioned by way of this Appeal.

7) Considering the record and rival submissions, it is evident that, even though the Complainant alleged that she had cancelled the MoU, P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL379.2023.doc.doc notice to that effect was not issued by her to the accused.
Similarly, despite the cheque of considerable amount was dishonoured, she did not issue the statutory demand notice to accused persons.
From the MoU it is evident that, the prospective returns were highly excessive.
In the said Application itself the Complainant has stated that, the representations made by the accused persons were malicious.
Thus, since inception the Complainant knew the aforesaid facts yet she entered into subject transaction and the MoU.
Therefore, it cannot be said that, the accused persons deceived the Complainant and dishonestly induced her to enter into the said MoU.

On the contrary, from a careful reading of the MoU it seems that, the Complainant entered into the said transaction on her own, willingly and after understanding its minute details only to earn an exorbitant interest knowingly taking risk of her money.
Therefore, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune has rightly held that, this is a civil dispute.

8) In so far as the reported cases cited by the learned Advocate for the Complainant are concerned,
the facts of the said cases and the case in hand are distinct and therefore those are of no help to him.
8.1) In view thereof, we find no illegality in the impugned Order.
As a result, the Appeal is liable to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
(SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.)
